chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rubay ibn Abdallah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

Knowledge is of two kinds: A knowledge with Allah which is hidden, no one from His creation has seen into it; and a knowledge which He taught His angels and His messengers. So as for that which He taught His angels and messengers, then it will occur. He does not belie Himself, nor His angels, nor His messengers. As for the hidden knowledge with Him, then He brings forward from it what He wills, and puts back from it what He wills, and establishes what He wills.

key_terms.بَدَاءٌ: Divine Alteration/Change (implied by context of bringing forward/delaying)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between hidden divine knowledge and revealed knowledge in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the absolute, uncreated knowledge of Allah known only to Him and the revealed knowledge granted to angels and messengers, which is inherently certain to occur. The former category is subject to 'Bada'' (divine alteration), allowing Allah to bring forward, delay, or establish events according to His will, a concept central to Shia theology regarding the interplay between divine decree and human agency. This narration underscores that while prophetic knowledge is fixed, the ultimate unfolding of destiny remains within the sovereign prerogative of God.
